name: Eyelid glue

card.summary: Cosmetic adhesive that sticks the lid skin into a temporary crease; little published research exists on the product itself.
card.note: Applied next to the eye; no studies specific to the glue were found.

quick.overview:
Eyelid glue is a cosmetic adhesive used to fix the upper lid skin into a fold, producing a temporary double eyelid. It serves the same goal as eyelid tape and is a non-surgical alternative to double eyelid surgery.

The sources reviewed contain no published studies of the glue itself, so what is known comes from background on double eyelid surgery and the cosmetic goal behind it.
quick.mechanism: A thin layer of adhesive holds a fold of lid skin in place so that a crease shows when the eye is open. The effect lasts until the glue is removed or wears off.
quick.risks: No clinical studies of eyelid glue were found. Any adhesive used next to the eye raises general questions of skin and eye irritation, which have not been specifically studied for these products in the sources reviewed.

lead: Eyelid glue is a cosmetic adhesive applied to the upper eyelid to hold the skin in a fold, giving the appearance of a double eyelid for a limited time. It is a non-surgical alternative to double eyelid surgery, which creates a permanent crease [1].
No published clinical studies of eyelid glue were located. This article therefore describes the aesthetic context only and does not assess the product's effects.

paras: A double eyelid is an upper lid with a visible crease. Wikipedia reports natural prevalence of about 41% among Koreans and roughly 70 to 83% among Chinese and Japanese people, and describes double eyelid surgery as among the most common cosmetic procedures in Taiwan and South Korea. The first recorded operation was performed in Japan in 1896 [1]. Surgical options include non-incisional suture methods, which are quicker but may fade, and incisional methods, which are described as longer-lasting [1]. Temporary products such as glue and tape provide a reversible alternative.
